name: Rogue's Passage
oracle_text:
{T}: Add {C}.
{4}, {T}: Target creature can't be blocked this turn.
blocked_sentences: {4}, {T}: Target creature can't be blocked this turn.

needs.what: a resolution op that makes a chosen creature unable to be blocked at all until end of turn -- an until-end-of-turn, per-object 'can't be blocked' flag on the targeted creature (not on the granting permanent), read by combat.can_block for every would-be blocker
needs.why_existing_wont_do: The only 'can't be blocked' machinery is the `block_restriction` static effect, and it is unreachable three ways from an activated ability. (1) It lives in a printed static on a permanent, collected by `characteristics._battlefield_statics`, which walks `card_of(obj).abilities` only -- so it applies to whatever its `affects` filter matches, and `affects` may contain only `static_filter_keys` (printed characteristics); there is no key for 'the creature this ability targeted', so a static on Rogue's Passage cannot be aimed at the target. (2) It has no duration: a static is on while its source is on the battlefield, so it cannot expire 'this turn'. (3) `grant_ability` cannot smuggle one onto the target, because granted abilities are pointers read by `primitives.granted_abilities`, whose only consumers are in `triggers.py` -- `_battlefield_statics` never consults them, so a granted `block_restriction` would load clean and do nothing. `grant_keyword` has no matching keyword either: the evasion keywords available (menace, fear, intimidate, skulk, shadow, horsemanship, the landwalks) are all conditional restrictions on *which* creatures may block, and any of them would be an approximation of full unblockability.
